serialFormats.description: 2010-present: first two digits = year (10 = 2010), digits 3-4 = week of manufacture; 9-13 characters total (typically 10).
sources: PickHVAC — Trane HVAC Age: Serial Number Decoding (https://www.pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/trane/) — '1204' = week 4 of 2012
Parts Town — Trane Serial Number Lookup (https://www.partstown.com/cm/resource-center/guides/gd2/trane-serial-number-lookup)
Inspector Handbook — Decode Trane HVAC Serial Number (https://inspectorhandbook.com/hvac/trane) — serial 2415836472 = week 15 of 2024
Building Intelligence Center — Trane HVAC age (https://www.building-center.org/trane-hvac-age/)
notes: Date portion (YYWW) of the examples is stated by the cited decoders; the trailing characters of examples 1 and 3 are illustrative fillers used only as regex fixtures.

Collision: a 9-character serial made in 2020-2029 (e.g. '2415...') also matches the 2002-2009 one-digit-year rule (2002, week 41). Disambiguate on the nameplate: 2020+ units are R-410A or R-454B (A2L) with Symbio 700/ReliaTel and a modern QR-code plate; 2002-2009 units are R-22 (R-410A only on 2006-2009 designs) with ReliaTel/UCP. Week must be 01-53 under either reading.
No manufacturer document or warranty lookup was available to this builder; confidence capped at medium (two independent secondary decoders agree).

serialFormats.description: 2002-2009: 9-character serial; first digit = last digit of year (2 = 2002 ... 9 = 2009), digits 2-3 = week of manufacture.
sources: PickHVAC — Trane HVAC Age (https://www.pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/trane/) — 'serial starting 752 = built 2007, week 52'; 2002-2009 serials are 9 characters
Building Intelligence Center — Trane HVAC age (https://www.building-center.org/trane-hvac-age/) — format introduced 2002: 1st digit year, 2nd-3rd week
Parts Town — Trane Serial Number Lookup (https://www.partstown.com/cm/resource-center/guides/gd2/trane-serial-number-lookup) — 2002 serials start with 2, 2003 with 3, etc.
notes: Example 1's date prefix '752' is stated by PickHVAC; examples 2 and 3 apply the same rule (year digit + week) with illustrative filler characters — they are regex/rule fixtures, not photographed nameplates.

Collision: a serial starting with 2 could be 2002 or (if the modern 2010+ format) 2020-2029. Real 2002-2009 serials are 9 characters; modern ones are usually 10 or more. If both match, check the refrigerant on the plate (R-22 => 2002-2009) and the model design sequence letter.
One-digit year cannot distinguish 2007 from 1997 by itself, but 1997 serials start with the letter M (see letter-year format), so a leading digit is 2002-2009.

serialFormats.description: 1983-2001: serial begins with a letter = year (W 1983 ... Z 2001), digits 2-3 = week of manufacture; 9 characters typical (8-10 accepted).
sources: Building Intelligence Center — Trane HVAC age (https://www.building-center.org/trane-hvac-age/) — 1983-2001 style: letter = year, positions 2-3 = week
PickHVAC — Trane HVAC Age (https://www.pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/trane/) — W=1983, X=1984, Y=1985, S=1986, B=1987 ... H=1993, J=1994 ... N=1998, P=1999, R=2000; K=1995

H2ouse / How To Look At A House — Trane furnace age (https://www.h2ouse.org/trane-furnace-age/, https://www.howtolookatahouse.com/Blog/Entries/2018/6/how-can-i-tell-the-age-of-a-trane-furnace-from-the-serial-number.html) — S = 1986 and Z = 2001 (out of alphabetical order; easily confused)
notes: K = 1995 (not 1990); 1990 is E. Letters A, I, O, Q, T, U, V are not used in this map.

S and Z are the out-of-order letters: two sources (h2ouse, howtolookatahouse, PickHVAC in one passage) give S = 1986 and Z = 2001; one search summary reversed them (Z = 1986, S = 2001). The pack follows the majority (S = 1986, Z = 2001). If the serial starts with S or Z, confirm with the model design sequence and plate style: 2001 units carry the 'Trane' swoosh-era plate and Voyager/Precedent model numbers; 1986 units are older designs.
Week is the two digits after the letter; a value above 53 means the serial is not this format.
Examples: the year letter and week digits are per the cited charts; the trailing characters are illustrative fillers (no dated nameplate photo was available).

serialFormats.description: 1980-1982 (approximate): the letter in the 3rd position from the end of the serial encodes the year (A/L/O = 1980, B/M/T = 1981, C/N/U = 1982); serial ends with two digits.
sources: PickHVAC — Trane HVAC Age (https://www.pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/trane/) — early-1980s units: letter 3rd from the end = year (A, L & O = 1980 / B, M & T = 1981 / C, N & U = 1982)
notes: LOW CONFIDENCE: only one secondary source describes this style and the overall length/structure of these serials is not documented; the regex is a best guess (ends in two digits, letter third from end). Month position was described as 'the 4th position in some formats' but could not be confirmed, so no month is decoded.
Examples are synthetic fixtures for the regex only. Treat any match as a hint: confirm age from the compressor date code, the nameplate style and the model design sequence.
Pre-1980 Trane serials and the American Standard '4th-position letter' style were not confirmed by any source available to this builder and are not decoded.

controls.name: Trane ReliaTel (RTRM refrigeration module with RTOM options, RTEM economizer, RTAM air-handling/VAV, RTDM dehumidification, RTVM ventilation, RTCI/TCI communication modules)
controls.description: Microprocessor control on Precedent 3-25 t, Voyager 12.5-25 t (2003+), Voyager III and Odyssey air handlers from about 2003 until replaced by Symbio 700 (2020s). No alphanumeric fault codes: diagnostics are shown by the RTRM green System LED (LED2), by the four LEDs on a zone sensor module (System / Heat / Cool / Service), and by the RTEM LED for the economizer. Full tables: Trane ReliaTel Service & Diagnostics manual (RT-SVD03) and the Trane Commercial Help Center 'List of Light Commercial LED Codes'.

faultCodes.meaning: Normal operation: RTRM powered, no active diagnostic.
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — List of Light Commercial LED Codes (support.trane.com article 360060172532)

faultCodes.meaning: No power to the RTRM or RTRM failed.
likelyCauses: No 24 VAC from TNS1 (blown secondary fuse, open primary)
checks: Measure 24 VAC at the RTRM 24 V input (transformer secondary); expect 20-28 VAC
Check TNS1 primary voltage tap matches line voltage and the low-voltage fuse
If 24 VAC is present at the board with LED2 dark, replace RTRM
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — List of Light Commercial LED Codes (support.trane.com article 360060172532)

faultCodes.meaning: One or more diagnostics present. Depending on unit configuration: supply fan failure, zone temperature sensor failure (CV units), programmable zone sensor (ZSM) communication failure, compressor lockout, defrost, gas heat, smoke detector, Frostat, communication, static-pressure or discharge-air-sensor diagnostic.
likelyCauses: Zone temperature sensor input failure on CV units (open/shorted ZTS wiring)
Compressor lockout after repeated HPC/LPC trips
Discharge-air / static-pressure sensor fault on VAV units
checks: Read the specific diagnostic: zone sensor LEDs (Heat / Cool / Service), the ReliaTel test-mode sequence, or a BAS/TCI or Trane service tool per help-center article 360060172412
Check the 10k zone sensor thermistor wiring (open or short to ground) before condemning the board
Check fan proving / dirty-filter switch inputs on the RTOM
Check HPC/LPC/limit/flame-sense history for the locked-out circuit
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — 'What can cause a 2 flash code on the RTRM?' (article 360038608131) and 'How do I retrieve fail codes from the RTRM when I have a 2 flash fault code?' (article 360060172412)

faultCodes.meaning: Unit is in TEST mode (LED2 pulses on and off while test mode is active).
checks: Remove the TEST 1 / TEST 2 jumper on the LTB; the unit exits test after about one hour on its own
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — List of Light Commercial LED Codes (support.trane.com article 360060172532)

faultCodes.meaning: Cooling failure: a compressor circuit is locked out (repeated HPC/LPC/compressor protection trips) — builder recollection of RT-SVD03, verify.
likelyCauses: HPC trips: dirty condenser, ODM failure, non-condensables, overcharge
Compressor internal overload / contactor / phase loss
checks: Identify which circuit is locked out (CPR1/CPR2) in test mode
Check refrigerant pressures, condenser coil, ODM operation, CC contactor and compressor amps
Reset lockout: cycle 24 V control power or switch the zone sensor mode to OFF and back
faultCodes.source: Builder memory of Trane ReliaTel Service & Diagnostics manual RT-SVD03 (zone sensor LED table) — not re-derived from the document
faultCodes.notes: LOW confidence entry; confirm against RT-SVD03 or the help-center LED list.

faultCodes.meaning: Heating failure (gas ignition lockout, limit trip or heat-pump defrost/heat diagnostic) — builder recollection of RT-SVD03, verify.
likelyCauses: Ignition control (IGN) lockout: dirty flame sensor, no gas, failed igniter
Combustion blower / pressure switch not proving
checks: Watch an ignition trial: CBM runs, pressure switch closes, spark/HSI, GV opens, flame sense microamps
Check filters, blower and TCO limits
Reset by cycling the mode or 24 V power
faultCodes.source: Builder memory of Trane ReliaTel Service & Diagnostics manual RT-SVD03 — not re-derived from the document
faultCodes.notes: LOW confidence entry; confirm against RT-SVD03.

faultCodes.code: Zone sensor SERVICE LED on steady

likelyCauses: Filter switch set point too low or tubing issue

faultCodes.source: Builder memory of Trane ReliaTel Service & Diagnostics manual RT-SVD03 — not re-derived from the document
faultCodes.notes: LOW confidence entry; confirm against RT-SVD03.

faultCodes.meaning: Supply fan failure (fan proving switch did not close after the fan was commanded on) — builder recollection of RT-SVD03, verify.
likelyCauses: Fan proving switch or tubing fault

faultCodes.notes: LOW confidence entry; confirm against RT-SVD03.

faultCodes.meaning: Economizer diagnostic present on the ReliaTel Economizer Module; the flash count identifies the fault (actuator, mixed-air/outdoor sensor, enthalpy/CO2 input). Full flash table: Trane help-center article 'LCU Economizer LED Codes (RTEM Module)'.
likelyCauses: Failed or out-of-range mixed-air sensor (MAS) or outdoor air sensor
Economizer actuator not driving / feedback fault
checks: Count the flashes and look up the code in help-center article 360037863611
Check sensor resistance (10k thermistor) and actuator travel in test mode step 'economizer'
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — '*LCU Economizer LED Codes? (RTEM Module)' (article 360037863611); flash-count table not transcribed
faultCodes.notes: Table not transcribed; only the existence and meaning of a flashing RTEM LED is recorded.

ledPatterns.pattern: RTRM LED2 (green System LED) steady on

ledPatterns.meaning: No 24 VAC to RTRM or board failed
checks: 24 VAC at RTRM power input
TNS1 secondary fuse

ledPatterns.pattern: RTRM LED2 two flashes every 2 s
ledPatterns.meaning: One or more diagnostics present — read them from zone sensor LEDs / test mode / service tool

diagnosticTips: TEST mode: momentarily short the TEST 1 and TEST 2 terminals on the low-voltage terminal board (LTB) for 2-3 seconds and remove the short; the unit enters step 1 (indoor fan). Each further momentary short advances one step (economizer, cool 1, cool 2, heat 1, heat 2 ... per unit configuration); holding the short in continuously auto-advances the steps. The unit leaves test mode about one hour after entry (per the UCP/ReliaTel IOM test-mode description). RTRM LED2 pulses while in test.
LEDs: RTRM System LED2 is on the RTRM board in the control box; zone sensor LEDs (System/Heat/Cool/Service) are on BAYSENS zone sensors that have LEDs.

Clearing lockouts: compressor and heat lockouts clear by cycling 24 V control power (open the unit disconnect for ~10 s) or by switching the zone sensor / thermostat mode to OFF and back; on BAS-connected units send the reset from Tracer.

Zone sensor input is a 10 kohm thermistor; an open or shorted ZTS gives a sensor-failure diagnostic (2-flash on LED2) and the RTRM falls back per its configuration. Check resistance at LTB before replacing the RTRM.
Full LED and diagnostic tables: Trane ReliaTel Service & Diagnostics Manual (RT-SVD03), ReliaTel user guide CNT-SVX15D-E4, and support.trane.com 'List of Light Commercial LED Codes'.

controls.name: Trane Symbio 700 unit controller
controls.description: Current-generation controller on Precedent 3-25 t, Voyager Commercial 27.5-50 t and Odyssey with Symbio (2019+). Descriptive alarms (no flash codes) shown on the onboard display and in the Symbio Service and Installation mobile app (Bluetooth); BACnet/Modbus and Tracer SC+ integration. Alarm names are text strings; the full diagnostic table is in the Symbio 700 application guides (BAS-SVP062 Precedent, BAS-APG048 Voyager Commercial).

faultCodes.meaning: Emergency stop input active — the unit shuts down all operation while the emergency-stop binary input is in the stop state (help-center article 'Symbio 700 Emergency stop').
likelyCauses: Field emergency-stop contact open (or jumper removed) at the Symbio 700 binary input
Smoke detector / fire alarm relay wired into the emergency stop input
checks: Verify the emergency-stop input state on the display or app (Status > Inputs)
Check the field contact / jumper on the low-voltage terminal strip and the smoke detector relay
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — Symbio 700 Emergency stop (article 18777598342029)

faultCodes.meaning: Symbio 700 reports gas-heat diagnostics with an alarm indicator status (e.g. ignition lockout, heat failure) in its Gas Heat section — application manual 'Gas Heat; Diagnostics and Alarm Indicator Status'. Exact alarm text depends on unit configuration.
likelyCauses: Ignition control lockout after failed trials (flame sense, gas supply, igniter)
Combustion blower / pressure switch not proving
checks: Open Alarms on the display/app and read the alarm text and time stamp
Run an ignition trial from Service > Test mode and watch CBM, pressure switch, GV and flame current
faultCodes.source: Trane Symbio 700 Controller Application Manual — Gas Heat; Diagnostics and Alarm Indicator Status (ManualsLib 3011763 p.54)
faultCodes.notes: Alarm strings not transcribed; consult the application guide for the table.

diagnosticTips: Reset alarms: Symbio Service and Installation app > Alarms > Reset Diagnostics; or onboard display > Service > Diagnostics > Reset Diagnostics (help-center).

The onboard display and the mobile app (Bluetooth pairing from the controller) show active/historical alarms with plain-language text and suggested resolutions; use the app for setpoints, test mode and configuration.
Symbio 700 alarms are text strings, not numeric codes; record the exact alarm text and time stamp for tech support (support.trane.com asks for the unit serial).
Full alarm tables: Symbio 700 Application Guide for Precedent (BAS-SVP062C-EN) and Voyager Commercial 27.5-50 t (BAS-APG048C-EN); Precedent IOM with Symbio 700 (RT-SVX077B-EN).

controls.name: Trane Voyager UCP (Unit Control Processor) microcontrols, pre-2003
controls.description: Legacy microprocessor on Voyager I/II/III (3-50 t) rooftops built roughly 1990-2003 before ReliaTel. Single red status LED on the UCP visible through a peep hole in the lower left corner of the control box cover; diagnostics via zone sensor LEDs and test mode. Full manual: Voyager Microcontrols (UCP) Service & Diagnostic Manual (support.trane.com).

faultCodes.meaning: UCP is functioning correctly with power applied.
faultCodes.source: Trane Voyager Commercial Installation & Operation manual — Starting the Unit / Test Modes (ManualsLib 825268 p.72); Voyager Microcontrols (UCP) Service & Diagnostic Manual (support.trane.com article 360060620431)

checks: Remove the short from the TEST terminals; the UCP exits test mode after about one hour in any step
faultCodes.source: Trane Voyager Commercial Installation & Operation manual — Test Modes (ManualsLib 825268 p.72)

faultCodes.meaning: UCP not powered or failed (LED glows whenever the UCP is functioning with power applied).
likelyCauses: No 24 VAC (TNS1 secondary fuse, primary tap)
checks: Check 24 VAC at the UCP power terminals; if present with LED dark, replace the UCP
faultCodes.source: Trane Voyager Commercial Installation & Operation manual — Test Modes (ManualsLib 825268 p.72) (inverse of the 'glows if functioning' statement)

diagnosticTips: TEST mode: short across the TEST terminals on the unit low-voltage terminal board (LTB) for 2-3 seconds and remove; the UCP LED blinks and step 1 turns on the indoor fan motor (IDM). Each following momentary short advances the step; the unit may be left in any step for up to one hour, after which the UCP exits test mode.
The red UCP LED is visible through the peep hole in the lower left corner of the control box cover without removing the cover.

Zone sensor LEDs (System/Heat/Cool/Service) on BAYSENS sensors report the same failure classes as ReliaTel (heat failure, cooling failure, dirty filter/fan failure) — see the UCP Service & Diagnostic Manual for the table.
Clear lockouts by cycling 24 V control power or switching the zone sensor mode to OFF and back.

controls.name: Trane IntelliPak UCM module controls with Human Interface (legacy)
controls.description: Module-based control on IntelliPak I rooftops (20-130 t) before Symbio 800: RoofTop Module (RTM, 1U48), Heat module, compressor modules, VAV/exhaust modules and the unit-mounted Human Interface (HI, 1U65) LCD keypad that displays plain-text diagnostics and status. Diagnostics are text messages, not numeric codes. Full list: IntelliPak Programming, Troubleshooting manual and IOM RT-SVX36.

faultCodes.code: HI COMMUNICATIONS FAILURE - CHECK INTERPROCESSOR COMM LINK
faultCodes.meaning: The unit-mounted Human Interface (HI, 1U65) is not communicating with the RoofTop Module (RTM, 1U48).
likelyCauses: Loose or damaged interprocessor communication (IPC) link wiring between HI and RTM
checks: Check the IPC bus connections at the HI and RTM (polarity, shield, terminations)
Verify RTM power LED and module DIP/address settings
Cycle power and watch whether HI re-establishes communication
faultCodes.source: Trane Commercial Help Center — IntelliPak (Legacy) HI Comm Loss (article 19893668115853)

faultCodes.meaning: The RTM has lost communication with the Heat Module.

sequenceOfOperation: Cooling (ReliaTel): on Y1/zone-sensor cooling demand the RTRM starts the IDM (immediately or per fan mode), then — if an RTEM economizer is fitted and outdoor conditions are suitable — modulates the economizer first; when the economizer cannot satisfy the load, the RTRM closes CC1 to start CPR1 (and ODM) after the minimum off-timer; Y2 / further demand brings on CPR2 via CC2. HPC/LPC trips are counted per cooling cycle; repeated trips lock out that compressor until reset.

Heating (gas, ReliaTel): on W1 the RTRM energizes the ignition control (IGN); the combustion blower (CBM) starts and the pressure switch must prove; after prepurge the igniter sparks and the gas valve (GV) opens; flame sensor (FS) must prove within the trial time or IGN retries then locks out (heat-failure diagnostic). Indoor fan starts after the heat fan-on delay; TCO limits open the ignition circuit on overtemperature. W2 stages the second heat stage / high fire.
Heat pump: RTRM energizes the reversing valve solenoid in the cooling mode (Trane 'O' logic), defrost by demand/time via the defrost control; electric heat staged via W1/W2 with the compressor.

Ventilation / economizer: RTEM drives the economizer actuator to minimum position when the fan runs occupied; free cooling enabled by dry-bulb or enthalpy (OHS) comparison; CO2 demand-controlled ventilation via RTVM when fitted.
notes: Designators CPR, CC, ODM, IDM, TNS, HPC, LPC are transcribed from the legend of Trane wiring diagram 1213-4333 (Trane eLibrary); the remaining designators are from builder memory of the Precedent ReliaTel wiring manual and must be confirmed against the diagram printed on the unit (drawing number on the control-box door).

3-phase scroll compressors on 208-230/460/575 V units are rotation-sensitive: verify rotation at start-up (suction/discharge pressures, noise); Trane fits a phase monitor on many 3-phase ReliaTel/Symbio units — check for a 'PM' / phase-monitor relay on the diagram before assuming.

Symbio 700 units: the controller replaces RTRM/RTOM/RTEM functions on one board with expansion modules; thermostat interface is via the Symbio 700 low-voltage terminals (R/G/Y1/Y2/W1/W2) or zone sensor; BACnet MS/TP directly on the controller.

sequenceOfOperation: The RTM (1U48) receives zone/discharge-air/static setpoints, stages compressors through the compressor modules, controls economizer and VAV supply fan (VFD or IGV) and reports status/diagnostics to the Human Interface (1U65) and BAS.
notes: IntelliPak uses numeric-prefixed designators (1U48, 4S12 ...) keyed to the schematic sheet; always read the legend on the unit's own diagram. Only designators confirmed by the cited sources are listed.

commonIssues.symptom: RTRM System LED2 flashing 2 times every 2 s; unit running but zone complains
likelyCauses: Zone temperature sensor wiring open/shorted (10k thermistor) — very common
Supply fan proving / dirty filter input
checks: Ohm the ZTS at the LTB (about 10 kohm at 77 F)
Read the specific diagnostic through zone sensor LEDs / test mode / service tool
Check fan proving and filter switches and their tubing

commonIssues.symptom: Economizer stuck open or closed, high humidity / high supply temperature, RTEM LED flashing
likelyCauses: Failed RTEM module or economizer actuator
checks: Run test mode to the economizer step and watch actuator travel
Check MAS/OAS resistance and the RTEM flash code
Verify minimum position setpoint and the OA changeover setting

commonIssues.symptom: No cooling, Cool LED flashing / compressor locked out
likelyCauses: Dirty condenser or failed ODM (HPC trips)
Phase loss or reverse rotation on 3-phase scroll
checks: Pressures and superheat/subcooling per circuit
ODM operation and condenser cleanliness
CC coil voltage and contacts, compressor amps vs RLA
Reset by cycling 24 V power and observe the next trip
sources: Builder field-pattern summary; lockout behaviour per help-center 2-flash article

commonIssues.symptom: Gas heat will not light or locks out intermittently (Heat LED flashing)
likelyCauses: Combustion pressure switch not closing (blocked flue/inducer, cracked tubing)
High-limit TCO tripping on low airflow (dirty filters, belt slip)
checks: Watch a full ignition trial in test mode heat step
Flame current, manifold pressure, pressure-switch differential
Filters, belt tension and blower amps
sources: Builder field-pattern summary; ignition sequence per ReliaTel gas/electric IOM RT-SVX21

commonIssues.symptom: Supply fan failure diagnostic (Service LED flashing) or unit shuts down on airflow
likelyCauses: VFD fault on VAV / SZVAV units
checks: Belt condition and tension, sheave alignment
Motor amps and bearing noise
Fan proving switch closure with fan running
VFD fault log

commonIssues.symptom: Water in the unit / condensate overflow shutdown
checks: Clear and flush the drain; verify trap depth against unit negative pressure
Check the overflow switch and reset

commonIssues.symptom: Human Interface shows 'HI COMMUNICATIONS FAILURE' or module communication failures
checks: Inspect the IPC bus wiring at each module and the HI
Check module power LEDs and addresses

notes: Web research for this pack was limited to search-engine summaries; WebFetch was unavailable, so the IOM nomenclature pages and the ReliaTel diagnostic tables could not be read in full. Entries marked 'builder memory' or evidence 'inferred' were not re-derived from a document and must be verified before relying on them.
Serial number decoding: 2010+ YYWW, 2002-2009 YWW, 1983-2001 letter+WW — all three from agreeing secondary decoders (no manufacturer document), hence medium. The 1980-1982 style is low.
Model nomenclature beyond digit 8 (heating capacity, options) is only partially decoded; read heat input, MCA/MOP and charge from the nameplate.

Refrigerant defaults: R-22 through the early-2000s designs; R-410A on Precedent 3-10 t from 2006 and 12.5-25 t / IntelliPak by 2010; R-454B (A2L) on 2025+ Precedent/Odyssey designs — always confirm from the plate.
Compressor Protection Module (CPM) could not be confirmed as a Trane light-commercial component name; not included.
